newsitem.title: FRANCE: Papandreou warns Albania troubles may spread.
newsitem.headline: Papandreou warns Albania troubles may spread.

text.p: Greek Deputy Foreign Minister Georges Papandreou, whose country borders Albania, has warned that trouble there could spread through the Balkans.

Asked in an interview published on Thursday by the newspaper Le Monde if he believed the crisis could spread outside Albania's borders, Papandreou replied: "Yes...and we Greeks want the crisis contained within the borders of Albania and not to spread to the ex-Yugoslav Macedonia, to Bulgaria or to Kosovo.

"We have also asked (Albanian President Sali) Mr Berisha to make sure the Greek minority in southern Albania not be involved in this conflict which is none of its concern. In times of crisis, minorities are too often chosen as sacrificial lambs," he said.
Papandreou said Europe should encourage Berisha to introduce more democracy and open talks with all political forces towards a coalition government.

The interview was published as Albanian government troops battled armed insurgents in southern Albania while the West hastily prepared a diplomatic drive to calm the fury unleashed in Europe's poorest country by the collapse of speculative investment schemes.
